svg.text: Resilience test harness: architecture and code structure
Part 1 shows how the classes are organised now. Part 2 shows which files changed and how.
PART 1 · HOW THE CODE IS ORGANISED NOW
fault, what to measure, pass criteria
machines, driver to use, time limits
Runs the same nine phases for every test. Contains no fault-specific code.
Safety: every fault is recorded before it is applied and can be undone
RunContext: the only access fault classes have to the test run
What the test does for this fault: how recovery
starts and what extra to measure.
How the fault is applied to the machine and
OsSshProcessDriver uses one small class per fault:
The only code that is specific to PostgreSQL.
PostgreSQLAdapter inherits from the base class and
from three method groups (mixins). Each group
holds the methods for one topic, in its own file.
Measurements are checked against the pass criteria. A value that cannot be measured is reported as "not measured" and fails.
subclass that is also a base class (bold border)
inherits from (points to the base class)
• the nine phases and the code for each fault in one file
• 12 checks of the fault name and 3 fixed lists of fault names
• adding a fault meant editing this file in several places
• base.py: FaultBehaviour, HeldFault, registration of fault classes
• one class, OsSshProcessDriver, for five faults
• 15 checks of the fault name inside its methods
• the orchestrator set the driver's fields one by one
• OsSshProcessDriver + one small class per fault (_ProcessKill, ...)
• os_ssh.py (new): SSH functions shared by both SSH drivers
• the orchestrator passes the settings in one call: configure(...)
• one class, PostgreSQLAdapter, with 58 methods for every fault type
Measurements for held faults and alerts
Measurements for held faults and alerts
• no support for a fault applied for a set time and then removed
• no common way to check monitoring alerts
• analysis/degradation.py (new): compares throughput and latency during the
fault with the baseline (e.g. 70% of baseline TPS).
• observability/alerts.py (new): asks the monitoring system whether an alert fired.
No monitoring system is connected yet, so alert checks report "not measured".
